chunks: Allah had informed you about the hypocrites with what He informed you, and described them with what He described them to you,
then they remained after him (peace be upon him), so they drew near to the leaders of misguidance and the callers to the Fire through falsehood and slander,
so they assigned them the duties, and made them over the heads of the people, and consumed the world through them,
and indeed the people are with the kings and the world, except whom Allah protects, so this is one of the four.
ai.seo_question: How did hypocrites gain power after the Prophet according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi highlights the historical continuity of the Munafiqun (hypocrites) who, after the Prophet's era, aligned with the 'leaders of misguidance' (often interpreted in Shia tradition as the Umayyad caliphs) through deceit, thereby securing administrative control and worldly dominance. This passage underscores the Shia theological view that political authority was often usurped by those lacking spiritual purity, illustrating the general human tendency to follow temporal power unless divinely protected.
